transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

For the past two weeks, I've been struggling with these awful, intrusive memories and flashbacks of a traumatic event that happened. It honestly feels like I'm reliving it all over again, and I just can't get the images out of my head. It's causing me so much distress and I really don't know what to do anymore.
I am sorry you are going through this. Could you tell me exactly how many days or weeks ago did this traumatic event take place?
The traumatic event happened exactly two weeks ago. These symptoms started almost immediately after it occurred, and I've been struggling with them every day since then.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports experiencing symptoms for exactly two weeks following a traumatic event. According to the DSM-5 criteria, Acute Stress Disorder is diagnosed when symptoms persist for three days up to one month after trauma exposure. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) requires symptoms to persist for more than one month. Given the current duration of two weeks, Acute Stress Disorder is the appropriate diagnosis, and PTSD is no longer a candidate.
